dialogue.Introduction: I am a Dryad, and I have watched over these trees since before anyone thought to name them. You may call me the Dryad, and I shall call you @, since that is the name the wind carries up to me.$h#$b#The mountain is quiet with us. Stay a while and listen to it.
dialogue.Mon: Good morning, @. The spring pollen has settled, so the air smells sweet today.$h
dialogue.Tue: The Guide came up the path this morning with a map of the mines. He keeps trying to show me where the bats are, as if I did not already know.$u
dialogue.Wed: Wednesday. Every day is the same to a tree, but I try to notice them anyway, @. It is good practice for a person.$h
dialogue.Thu: The Merchant offered to buy the moss off my tent poles. I said the moss was not for sale. He said everything is for sale. I said the moss disagreed.$a
dialogue.Fri: Fridays bring travelers up the mountain path. Some of them even remember to greet the trees before they greet me.$h
dialogue.Sat: The Nurse says I ought to sleep in a proper bed. I told her I sleep in the roots of the mountain. She said that is how people get stiff.$s
dialogue.Sun: A quiet Sunday. The seeds on my tent flap are starting to sprout, and I am being very patient about it.$h
dialogue.Mon2: Good day to you. The mountain path is steep, but you took it well enough.$h
dialogue.Tue2: I hope the rain stays off the road today. Rain is good for the roots, but hard on the feet.
dialogue.Thu2: Hm. You have dirt on your boots, @. That is the best kind of dirt. It has been where things grow.$h
dialogue.Sat2: The mountain fog has come in. I like it. It makes the valley look like a half remembered dream.
dialogue.Mon4: Ah, @. You have been climbing up here more often lately. I notice these things, even if I rarely say so.$h#$b#Thank you for coming to see me.$l
dialogue.Tue4: The Clothier once came up here to ask whether the trees were haunted. I told him only the skeletons were. He did not laugh, and I thought that a shame.$s
dialogue.Wed4: My roots reach far under the valley. Sometimes I feel the pickaxes in the mines like a headache, very far below.$s
dialogue.Thu4: The Painter likes to sit under my oldest branch and sketch. His paintings are not very accurate, but they are kind.$h
dialogue.Fri4: Do you know what I miss most? The old forest before the farms. Nothing hurried about it. The rivers simply ran where they pleased.$s
dialogue.Sat4: The Tavernkeep sends a bottle of mead up the path now and then. I pretend to disapprove. Then I drink it.$h
dialogue.Sun4: Sundays are when I most like to sit still. Each of my leaves catches a little sunlight, and I catch a little of you. That is enough for me.$l
dialogue.Mon8: I was not always calm, @. Once I was a fierce guardian of the jungle, and I turned away anyone who threatened the trees. Some days I still feel that fire.$s#$b#I am glad it has cooled. Your company has helped.$h
dialogue.Tue8: Sometimes I think the valley would fall to pieces without you. You plant, you harvest, you fight whatever crawls out of the mines. That is a lot for one farmer to carry.$s
dialogue.Wed8: I dreamed of the moon last night, the way it looked when the trees were young. It was lovely, and it frightened me a little.$s#$b#I would rather not be frightened alone, so please stay for a while.$l
dialogue.Thu8: I trust you, @. I rarely say that to anyone. The forest does not hand out trust to strangers, and I was a stranger for a very long time.$h
dialogue.Fri8: The Stardrop Saloon gave me a fine evening once, and then the Wizard sent me a letter about a dark shadow in the woods. I have not decided which story I prefer.$u
dialogue.Sat8: I used to fear that nothing I grew would last. Then I met you and your farm, and it occurred to me that a garden is the most honest kind of hope there is.$l
dialogue.Sun8: Tell me about the farm when you were small. I know you have a past. Everyone does, even trees, which keep theirs written in rings.$h
dialogue.Wed6: Wednesday afternoons the Painter comes up with his easel and asks me to hold still. I am a tree, @. I am not very good at moving anyway.$h
dialogue.Fri6: The Mechanic has been fixing the tram lines below, and every time a gear turns the branches shake. I wish they would ask first.$a
dialogue.Sun6: I have been thinking about the Calico Desert. Nothing grows there unless someone is patient. Perhaps I should visit and teach the cacti a thing or two.$h
dialogue.Mon10: You have a true feel for growing things, @. Few people can make a seed listen. Keep tending that garden, and never let it go wild.$h
dialogue.Wed10: I want you to know something. When the Eye of Cthulhu came, I was afraid for the trees. You stayed by the mountain when others fled. I will remember that always.$l
dialogue.Fri10: The next time you walk into the Skull Cavern, carry a seed with you and plant it near the entrance. That place needs a little green to remember the sun.$h
dialogue.Tue10: You visit the Calico Desert often, I think. If you find a cactus flower, bring it back to me. I would like to see what the sand has made.$h
dialogue.Sat10: The Old Man at the top of the mountain asked me once what a farmer is. I told him a farmer is someone who listens to the seasons. I think you are a good one.$h
dialogue.Sun10: Our valley is small, but it is full of stubborn roots. That is why I love it, @. Nothing here gives up without a fight, and nothing here stays alone.$l
dialogue.spring_Mon: Spring has climbed the mountain at last. The first buds on my branches have opened, and I feel like singing, which I rarely do.$h
dialogue.summer_Wed: Summer heat hangs heavy on the mountain. The insects are loud, and so am I, complaining about them all afternoon.$a
dialogue.fall_Fri8: Autumn leaves are falling everywhere, @. I think they come down so the roots can rest. I like to believe that is what I am doing too.$l
dialogue.winter_Sun: Snow on the mountain makes everything very still. Even a Dryad needs a blanket in winter. Do not tell anyone I said so.$s
dialogue.spring_Mon4: Early spring, and the spirit of the valley is waking. Walk the grass slowly, @. It is listening.$h
dialogue.summer_Sat6: Sit with me in the summer shade. The Guide keeps warning me the river is dangerous. I tell him the river is only the river.$h
dialogue.fall_15: Harvest season is half over, and the trees are turning. Remember to eat something sweet before the cold comes.$h
dialogue.winter_20: A cold night. I have thought about the moon again. It keeps watch over us all, and I think it would like to see you smile.$h
dialogue.spring_Tue: A squirrel stole a seed from my tent this morning. I forgave it, because it looked so proud of itself.$h
dialogue.winter_Thu10: The fire in the Guide's hut has gone out, and he is asking everyone for kindling. I am a tree and have none to spare, but I wish him warm dreams.$h

rainy: Rain on the mountain is the one time I let my hair down. Literally. The leaves drink it, and so do I, in my way.$h

situations.eye: The Eye has closed at last, @. I felt its gaze on the mountain for weeks, and now the trees can breathe again.$h
situations.evilBoss: The Eater of Worlds or the Brain of Cthulhu is gone, whichever it was. The corruption beneath my roots has gone quiet for once.$s
situations.skeletron: Skeletron is defeated and the dungeon door stands open. The Old Man is free. I hope nothing down there tries to bargain with you.$u
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee has fallen. Her hive smells of honey all the way up the mountain, and the bees keep humming, a little confused.$h
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh has fallen and hardmode has begun. The Hallow is spreading through the valley like sunlight through leaves, and the new monsters are stronger than before. Be careful, @.$s
situations.mechs: One of the mechanical bosses was destroyed last night. The metal screeching stopped, and I slept better than I have in weeks.$h
situations.plantera: Plantera is defeated. The jungle temple is open now, and I can feel the old jungle again. It is a joy.$h
situations.golem: The Golem is destroyed. The temple stone cracked and sunlight poured through the roots. I cried a little, and I am not sorry for it.$s
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist has fallen and the celestial pillars rise into the sky. I can hear them humming like a great chorus of stars.$u
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord has been defeated. The sky is finally quiet, and the stars look down on us as if they are relieved too.$h
situations.goblins: We repelled a goblin army last night. Their clanking rang across the valley for hours. The Goblin Tinkerer is very proud of the bang.$h
situations.pirates: The pirates came ashore and were sent packing. The Pirate is scrubbing sand from his boots this morning and complaining loudly.$h
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion has been repelled. Snow still clings to the ridge, and my roots have frozen half solid.$s
situations.martians: The Martian Madness has been repelled. Their strange machines left scorch marks in the grass, and the trees are still angry about it.$a
situations.bloodMoon: There was a blood moon last night. I stood on the mountain and watched it, and the trees pulled in close and whispered all night.$s
situations.eclipse: The sun went dark for a while last night. The valley went cold and quiet, and I counted the stars until the light came back.$u
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today, and the whole town is invited. I am told the music will carry all the way up the mountain. My branches are already swaying.$h

festivals.spring13: The Egg Festival is here, @. I hid a painted egg among my roots, and the Painter is sure to find it. I hope you do too.$h
festivals.spring24: The Flower Dance is tonight. Wear something green and come find me in the meadow. I will show you the step the old trees taught me.$h
festivals.summer11: The Luau feeds the whole valley. Bring something for the community soup, and I will bring a bowl of mountain herbs that tastes of home.$h
festivals.summer28: Tonight is the Dance of the Moonlight Jellies on the beach. The jellies glow like little lanterns of the sea. Come watch them with me.$l
festivals.fall16: The Stardew Valley Fair is on. The grange displays are lovely this year, and I have entered my finest pinecone. Wish me luck.$h
festivals.fall27: It is Spirit's Eve, and the maze is full of shadows. I am not frightened of ghosts, but the scarecrows in that maze give me chills.$u
festivals.winter8: The Festival of Ice is here. The ice fishing contest is noisy and the snow sculptures are beautiful. I built a small snow tree, and it leans, like me.$h
festivals.winter25: Feast of the Winter Star. I have a secret gift for someone in town and will not say who. Keep your eyes open, @.$h

loved.text: Ahh. A flower still wearing its roots. You have a good eye, @.$h

liked.text: Lovely. The bees will be pleased with this one.$h

neutral.text: Hm. Not a plant, but I will allow it.

disliked.text: Metal and smoke. Take it away from my roots.$a

hated.text: Burn it, and do not tell me where the ashes went.$a

help: Bit of help here? These thorns are not sharing.
Someone cut these vines off me, quickly please.
Could use a hand over here. Mind the bees.
thanks: Thank you, @. A debt to a tree is repaid in leaves and shade.$h
I would have ended in the thorns without you. The forest remembers this, @.$l
battle: Roots, rise! Show this beast the patience of trees!
Bees, sting! Now, for the old oak, charge!
courage.hurt: I am bruised and needle-sore. Let me rest among my roots until the sap rises again.$s

danger.boss: A great beast stirs in the deep woods, @. The trees are shuddering. I will stand and fight.$a
danger.invasion: Pirates and goblins in my grove. They will learn that roots grip tighter than any hook.$a
danger.pumpkinMoon: The pumpkin moon hangs low and the scarecrows whisper. I will keep watch with the vines.$h
danger.frostMoon: Frost creeps across the bark. The frost legion will find this forest is not so easily frozen.$h
danger.eclipse: The sun has gone out and the shadows crawl. Stay near the roots, @, and do not wander off.$s
danger.bloodMoon: The blood moon turns the leaves red. Something is wrong in these woods, and I intend to fix it.$a

events.after: Walk gently on the way back, @. The roots remember who stepped on them.

steps.say: Oh, hello, @. You came through the grove very quietly. Most travelers stomp about like bears.$h
I am the Dryad. I have kept this grove since before any fence or farm stood in the valley.#$b#The trees speak to me, and I speak back when they are polite.

steps.question: What brings you into the grove?

answers.reply: Then pass gently. The roots are listening even when you are not.$s

answers.text: I came to see the trees.
answers.reply: Good. Most people only look at the ore and the coins.$h

steps.say: Here, an acorn from the oldest oak. Plant it where the sun reaches, and be patient with it.$h
The forest has been quiet since the Eye fell. I think it is glad to have company again.$h

events.after: Come again tomorrow. The dew will be thick, and I will have something new to show you.

steps.say: @! Your breath is short. The mountain path is steep, but you climbed it anyway.$h
I rest up here most days. The wind is the only one who visits often, and he never stays long.#$b#Sit with me a moment if you can spare it.

steps.question: Do you ever feel lonely up here?

answers.reply: Then you and I are alike. Loneliness is only a root that has not found the others yet.$s

answers.text: Not at all. I like the quiet.
answers.reply: Quiet is good. It is the loud things that wear a body out.$h

steps.say: The Merchant asked me to sell him my moss. I told him the moss is not for sale, and neither is the mountain.$a
Still, I would like a proper friend. Someone who visits for something other than the view.$l

events.after: Mind the bats on your way home, @. The Guide says they bite only the ones who are rude.

steps.say: Ah, @. The night air is cool and the owls are gossiping. The Guide has followed you here, as Guides tend to do.$u
Greetings, Dryad. Did you know the wood here makes fine torches? I keep a book full of helpful hints, and this grove is my favorite chapter.$h
A helpful hint, from a man who has never once sat still for a whole night.$h
Sitting still is how you find the hints, friend. Now listen. A good forest guardian always checks the roots before the fire.$h

answers.text: You two make a fine pair.
answers.reply: We do, in our way. The Guide keeps me honest, and I keep him patient.$h
Quiet, says the farmer. The owls have something to say about that.$a

steps.say: The night is young. If you stay, the stars come out one by one, and I know all of their names.$h
Goodnight, Guide. Keep your book dry.$h

events.after: Keep your lantern lit on the way down, @. The mountain is darker than it looks.

steps.say: Oh, @. Come in, come in. Mind the moss by the door, it is delicate.$h

I have been thinking about what I was before the valley. I was a guardian with a temper, and I frightened even the bravest adventurers.#$b#Being calm is not something I was born with. I learned it slowly, from the trees.

steps.question: Do you ever think about your own past?

answers.reply: Then you understand. The past is a root we all drag along. Some days it is a comfort, and some days a weight.$s
Looking ahead is wise. I am still learning it, and you are teaching me.$h

steps.say: When the moon rose over the jungle, I felt so small I could not bear it. I am better now. I think you helped.$s
Would you sit beside me a little while? I do not like the dark when I think too much.$l
Thank you for listening, @. Some nights I only need someone to notice I am here. Tonight, you noticed.$h
Goodnight, @. Keep the lantern lit on your way home.$h

events.after: Now I must go before the Merchant finds out I have been giving things away for free.

steps.say: @, I did not expect to find you in the open field. The farm is bright today, and the crops stand very straight.$h
I have come to plant something, if you will allow it. A seed from the mountain, to grow beside your crops.$h
I know how hard you have worked here. The valley could not run without someone who gets up early and stays late.$l

answers.reply: Then the fence will have a leafy friend. Fences are lonely things without a little green.$h
Practical, as always. The shed will have a companion, then.$h

steps.say: This is my gift. A sunflower from the mountain. Let it face the sun each morning, and remember that you are worth turning toward.$l
